The tangents to the circle at $P$ and $Q$ meet at $T$. Let $A(\theta)$ denote the area of the region bounded by the chord $PQ$ and the minor arc $PQ$, and let $B(\theta)=PT+TQ-PQ$. hindi: माना कि $P$ तथा $Q$ वृत्त $x^{2}+y^{2}=1$ (केन्द्र $O$) पर दो बिन्दु इस प्रकार हैं कि $\angle POQ=\theta$, जहाँ $0<\theta<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ है। $P$ तथा $Q$ पर वृत्त की स्पर्श रेखाएँ $T$ पर मिलती हैं। माना कि $A(\theta)$ जीवा $PQ$ तथा लघु चाप $PQ$ से परिबद्ध क्षेत्र का क्षेत्रफल है, तथा $B(\theta)=PT+TQ-PQ$ है। तब $\displaystyle\lim_{\theta\to0^{+}}\dfrac{A(\theta)}{B(\theta)}$ बराबर है
solution: $OT$ bisects $\angle POQ$ and $OP\perp PT$, so $PT=TQ=\tan\dfrac{\theta}{2}$; also $PQ=2\sin\dfrac{\theta}{2}$
With $u=\dfrac{\theta}{2}$: $B=2(\tan u-\sin u)$, and $\tan u-\sin u=\dfrac{u^{3}}{2}+\dots$, so $B\approx u^{3}=\dfrac{\theta^{3}}{8}$
solution_full: Area of sector $OPQ$ is $\dfrac{\theta}{2}$ (radius 1) and area of triangle $OPQ$ is $\dfrac{1}{2}\sin\theta$. The region between chord $PQ$ and the minor arc is the sector minus the triangle, so $A(\theta)=\dfrac{\theta-\sin\theta}{2}$.

Since $OP\perp PT$, $OQ\perp QT$ and $OP=OQ$, the line $OT$ bisects $\angle POQ$. In right triangle $OPT$, $\angle POT=\dfrac{\theta}{2}$, so $PT=\tan\dfrac{\theta}{2}$, and similarly $TQ=\tan\dfrac{\theta}{2}$.
The chord is $PQ=2\sin\dfrac{\theta}{2}$. Hence, with $u=\dfrac{\theta}{2}$, $B(\theta)=2\tan u-2\sin u=2(\tan u-\sin u)$.
Expansions: $\tan u=u+\dfrac{u^{3}}{3}+\dots$ and $\sin u=u-\dfrac{u^{3}}{6}+\dots$, so $\tan u-\sin u=\dfrac{u^{3}}{2}+O(u^{5})$ and $B(\theta)=u^{3}+O(u^{5})=\dfrac{\theta^{3}}{8}+O(\theta^{5})$.
(Taking $B\approx\dfrac{\theta^{3}}{4}$, i.e. forgetting the half angle, gives $\dfrac{1}{3}$; taking $A\approx\dfrac{\theta^{3}}{6}$ gives $\dfrac{4}{3}$.)
originality_note: New: the two cubic-order 'defects' of a small circular arc (segment area against the excess of the tangent path over the chord) are compared, so the limit is read from the geometry before any expansion (way 5). Closest known: lim (tan x - sin x)/x^3 and Huygens/Snell arc approximations. Different because: the numerator is an area and the denominator a length excess of the tangent path, both built from the figure, and the half-angle must be found from the tangents.
blueprint_concepts: Evaluation of limit involving trigonometric functions

concept_use.Evaluation of limit involving trigonomet: The limit of A/B is a 0/0 trigonometric limit in theta, with tan(theta/2) and sin(theta/2) from the figure.
concept_use.Evaluation of limit using expansion: theta - sin theta ~ theta^3/6 and tan u - sin u ~ u^3/2 give the leading cubic terms of A and B.
